name: Bondage by the three guṇas
description: Bhagavad Gītā 14.5–9: sattva, rajas and tamas, born of prakṛti, bind the imperishable embodied one in the body — sattva by attachment to happiness and to knowledge, rajas by attachment to action, tamas by heedlessness, idleness and sleep; attachment to the guṇas causes births in good and bad wombs (13.22).
members: sattva: attachment to happiness (sukha-saṅga) and to knowledge (jñāna-saṅga)
antidotes: Seeing no agent but the guṇas and knowing what is beyond them (14.19)
Serving Kṛṣṇa with the unswerving yoga of devotion (14.26)

name: Ignorance veiling knowledge (ajñāna)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 13–14: what is other than the dispositions called knowledge is ignorance (13.12); tamas is born of ignorance and deludes all embodied beings (14.8); covering knowledge, tamas attaches to heedlessness (14.9); ignorance is the fruit of tamas and arises from it (14.16–17).

name: Attachment (saṅga)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: attachment to the guṇas is the cause of puruṣa's births in good and bad wombs (13.22); sattva binds by attachment to happiness and knowledge, rajas by attachment to action (14.6–7); those who have conquered the fault of attachment (saṅga-doṣa) reach the imperishable place (15.5); the aśvattha is cut with the weapon of non-attachment (15.3).

name: Delusion (moha)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 14–15: tamas deludes all embodied beings (14.8); delusion arises when tamas increases and comes from it (14.13, 14.17); the one gone beyond the guṇas neither hates nor longs for it (14.22); those free of pride and delusion reach the imperishable place (15.5); the deluded (vimūḍha) do not see the living being (15.10).

name: Greed (lobha)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 14.12, 14.17: greed arises when rajas increases, and comes from rajas.

name: The pairs of opposites (dvandva)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 15.5: those released from the pairs known as pleasure and pain go to the imperishable place; cf. the sameness toward pairs in 14.24–25.

name: Desire (kāma)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 15.5: those whose desires are turned away (vinivṛttakāma) go to the imperishable place.
